label: Koushun Takami — Battle Royale
description: Dystopian survival novel of coerced youth combat, state violence, media logic, and trust under extreme conditions.

label: RuneScape
description: MMORPG known for skill progression, quests, economy, persistent world, and long-form repetitive play loops.

label: Ocean’s Eleven
description: Ensemble heist film structured around specialists, planning, misdirection, and coordinated execution.

label: Cormac McCarthy — The Road
description: Post-apocalyptic journey pared to parent-child survival, moral persistence, ash landscape, and stripped prose.

label: Brandon Sanderson — Mistborn
description: Epic fantasy combining a failed-chosen-one premise, heist-team structure, hard magic, revolution, and industrial-age texture.

label: Brandon Sanderson
description: Fantasy writer known for explicit magic-system design, structural plotting, genre recombination, and large shared-world construction.

label: Brandon Sanderson — The Stormlight Archive
description: Long epic fantasy centered on returning magic, oaths, war, ecology, trauma, leadership, and interconnected worldbuilding.

label: Ann Leckie — Ancillary Justice
description: Space opera narrated by a former ship AI constrained to one body; identity, empire, embodiment, and distributed self.

label: Martha Wells — The Murderbot Diaries
description: SF series about an enslaved security construct that hacks itself free; autonomy, media, anxiety, labor, corporations, and personhood.

label: Martha Wells
description: SF/fantasy author whose anthropology interests and wide genre reading inform constructed cultures and Murderbot.

label: MMORPG / game-system culture
description: Persistent-world games normalize stats, levels, loot, quests, builds, classes, optimization, guilds, and systems literacy.

label: Reality TV / competition-show grammar
description: Elimination, confessionals, audience judgment, manufactured stakes, sponsorship, and spectacle as narrative machinery.

label: LitRPG / GameLit
description: Fiction that makes game mechanics, stats, progression systems, and interface logic explicit within narrative.

label: Matt Dinniman — Dungeon Crawler Carl
description: LitRPG satire combining dungeon crawl, death-game spectacle, game systems, streaming/reality-TV logic, apocalypse, and character-driven resistance.

label: Matt Dinniman
description: Author whose lifelong game-playing and web-serial/LitRPG context inform Dungeon Crawler Carl.

label: Joan Didion
description: Essayist/novelist who explicitly described learning sentence mechanics by typing Hemingway.

label: Ralph Ellison
description: Novelist/essayist who studied Hemingway, Joyce, Dostoevsky and Stein while developing his craft.

label: Ellison — Invisible Man
description: Novel of race, ideology, identity, performance, migration, and visibility using modernist, folkloric, and vernacular resources.

label: García Márquez — One Hundred Years of Solitude
description: Multigenerational novel of history, myth, memory, violence, repetition, and the marvelous within everyday reality.

label: Chinua Achebe — Things Fall Apart
description: Novel of Igbo society and colonial disruption, consciously engaging and correcting European representations of Africa.

label: Toni Morrison — Beloved
description: Novel of slavery’s afterlives, memory, haunting, motherhood, language, history, and the limits of representation.

label: American Western / frontier myth
description: Literary and cinematic tradition of frontier space, mobility, violence, law, settlement, individualism, and revisionist critique.
